posts.name: Snail Shell
posts.cooked:
Now that WotC is safely a thing, I'm sure the next question is how many more expansions will there be.  Villains seems to be another mega-expansion, which rocks.  I'm thinking more the regular expansions.

 

The math that I mention in the title comes from the Nemesis mechanic.  Four Heroes still lack a nemesis in the game (Absolute Zero, Bunker, Unity, and The Scholar), not counting Vengeance.  With two more regular expansions, we'd see four new heroes and eight new villains, bringing the total to eight each and seeing everyone get a nemesis.  Does that make sense?

 

Also, I joined the SotM bandwagon late.  Any chance there will be another design-a-baddie contest?

posts.name: MrLeRobot
posts.cooked:
If I may allow myself to take a huge wild guess on what could make the final expansion, I'd say this:

Campaign Mode

I saw a lot of fan made campaign for SotM. I even started creating my own sorta storyline to go through all of the villain, but with an added flavor, just for fun. I had a lot of fun just imagining how villains show up and why they're there and how the heroes would respond... I can't imagine Christopher NOT doing this kind of exercise. Thinking about it, I know he did. Heck, he's got like 30 years worth of storyline written down in his head (and also inside a notebook if I'm not mistaken?)... I know I'd personnally be all the way into a big multi-session campaign of SotM, with each match influencing the outcome of the rest of the whole story. Perhaps, there could even be some special cards, not included in a particular deck, with a special power a hero would start every game with, ala "Pathfinder Adventure Card Game"? You've beaten Ambuscade? "Hey, look how sweet those custom handguns look like..." Expatriette tells herself. "Maybe I should bring those to my next fight, 'cause you know, you never have too much guns...". Even the Big Bad could be a multi-match battle. Kind of like "You think you've beat me... Now, witness my true form and despair!"

Anyone?

One year ago, I began taking note on how a "campaign game" using cards could work. Heroes had varying skills (recruit, patrol, investigate, science, etc), and you used your recruited heroes to solve "problem" cards (Crime wave ! 3 patrol point to solve. Framed Hero ! But I never thought before to give this a "goal" like defeating a greater menace (maybe by building a big Doctor McGuffin's Neutralizer ?) or preventing FILTER or other organizations from doing something bad - a "scenario".

I certainly would like to see something like that published by >G someday :)
